summary: The note covers a set of local tax amendments passed by the City Council on October 3, 2023, which cut property tax, raise the hotel occupancy tax, and raise the local sales tax. It compares these changes with neighboring cities such as Granton, Rivertown, Lakeside City, Brookfield and Meadowlands. It also reports mixed resident and business reactions and an economist's call for the Council to monitor outcomes and stay flexible.
one_line: City Council's October 2023 tax overhaul lowers property tax but raises hotel and sales taxes, compared against neighboring cities and resident reactions.
key_facts: The City Council passed a sweeping series of local tax amendments in a session dating from October 3, 2023.
Council chair Marianne Delaney led the legislators in revising the city's tax code.
Effective January 1, 2024, the homeowner property tax rate falls from 1.5% to 1.3%.
The hotel occupancy tax rises from 10% to 12%, with funds meant for community infrastructure and public services.
The local sales tax rises by 1%, to 7%, to fund emergency services and public school improvements; local business owners have pushed back.
Councilwoman Sara Beckett called the sales tax increase "a necessary step to ensure our city's growth and maintain the high standard of living our residents are accustomed to."
Granton recently raised its property tax from 1.6% to 1.8%, citing emergency services and school funding.
Rivertown keeps a steady 1.4% property tax rate but lacks some of the progressive social programs the city offers.
Lakeside City raises its hotel tax only during peak travel seasons and keeps a 10% rate the rest of the year.
Brookfield and Meadowlands have a more modest 6% sales tax, making the city's increase among the highest in the region.
Retiree James Anderson approves of the property tax cut for those on fixed incomes, while parent Diane Matthews tentatively supports the sales tax increase if it benefits schools.
Dr. Gerald Huffman of the city's university said the Council should monitor economic feedback loops and remain agile in its fiscal strategy.
